note: Adapted from Hill's English original description of 1933. The original names it Calotermes (Cryptotermes) atratus, n. sp.; the type locality is near Appin, New South Wales, Australia, and it was also collected at Jamberoo. Many figures in the original measurement table are incomplete in the photocopy (body length including the wings, head length, antennal length, pronotum width and others); this entry transcribes only the legible items and notes the gaps here.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier head short and wide, widest in the posterior quarter, narrowing forwards to the anterior third and then widening forwards into the extremely thickened frontal rim; the rim deeply cleft in the middle and not projecting forwards over the vertical and distinctly rugose frontal surface. The lower anterior margin of the head not prolonged, and no horn-like process near the lateral margins of the postclypeus — in this it differs from the other known Australian species, all of which have a horn-like process on the anterior part of the head. Alate almost black throughout, distinctly darker than C. queenslandis; pronotum much wider than the head; wings short and of moderate width; tibial spur formula 3:3:3, the spurs long and moderately thick.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Colour as a whole similar to C. queenslandis but darker (almost black); antennae and legs (except the tarsi) dark brown, tarsi pale yellow. Head small, longer than wide, widest behind the compound eyes, the posterior margin hemispherical; compound eyes small, nearly triangular (diameter 0.185 mm); ocelli small, circular, very close to the compound eyes. Antennae 13- or 14-segmented: segment 1 short and thick, segment 2 about half the length of segment 1 and two thirds its width, segment 3 longer and wider than segment 2 with a widened apex, segment 4 usually shortest and narrowest, spherical or as long as segments 2 and 5, segment 5 usually longer and wider than segment 4 or the same as segment 4, segment 6 longer than segment 5, segments 7—12 increasing in length, segment 13 as long as segment 12, oval and much narrower than segment 12. Labrum about as long as wide, distinctly convex, the sides barely widening, the anterior margin truncate. Pronotum large, much wider than the head, strongly arched above, the anterior margin broadly concave, the anterolateral corners rounded, the sides nearly parallel, the posterolateral corners slightly oblique, the posterior margin slightly wavy; the posterior margins of the mesonotum and metanotum broad and nearly straight. Wings short and of moderate width: the subcosta of the fore wing very short (absent in the hind wing), usually shorter than the width of the wing at the suture; radius short, about one third of the wing length; radial sector giving off 7—9 branches towards the anterior margin; media very variable, usually thick at both ends, running above the anterior third of the wing, joining the radial sector at or behind the middle of the wing, sometimes reaching the wing apex or, after the first junction with the radial sector, forming a series of loops; cubitus running above the middle of the wing and giving off several branches towards the posterior margin. Wing membrane and veins densely covered with scale-like and minute spine-like microtrichia. Legs short and thick, with a few short hairs; tibial spurs long and moderately thick, 3:3:3. Measurements (mm): head width 0.92—0.99; fore wing length 6.00, width 1.66; hind tibia length 0.74; the remaining items (body length with and without the wings, head length, antennal length, pronotum length and width) are incomplete in the photocopy of the original and are not transcribed.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Mandibles, postclypeus, frons and frontal rim black; postmentum nearly black; anteclypeus white; labrum and antennae ochraceous yellow; palps and the rest of the head chestnut; pronotum chestnut, the anterior and posterior margins darker; the rest of the thorax, the abdomen and the legs ochraceous brown. Head with a fine shagreened sculpture, short and wide, widest in the posterior quarter, narrowing forwards to the anterior third and then widening forwards into the extremely thickened frontal rim; the rim deeply cleft in the middle and not projecting forwards over the vertical and distinctly rugose frontal surface; the lower anterior margin of the head not prolonged; no horn-like process near the lateral margins of the postclypeus. Antennae short and thick, 13-segmented: segment 1 short, only slightly longer than wide at its apex; segment 2 two thirds the length of segment 1 and also two thirds its width; segment 3 shortest, as wide as segment 2, with a swollen apex; segment 4 as wide as segment 3, rounded; segments 5—12 about as wide as segment 4, gradually slightly longer; segment 13 slightly shorter and narrower than segment 12. Mandibles (detached from the head) short and thick: the left mandible with 2 forward-pointing sharp teeth at the apical third, and behind them, between them and the large basal molar tooth, a short blunt tooth; the right mandible with one forward-pointing sharp tooth in the middle and, between it and the basal molar tooth, a larger and thicker tooth. Labrum large, wide at the base, narrowing towards the truncate apex. Postclypeus short and wide, about one quarter as long as wide; anteclypeus two thirds the length of the postclypeus, the sides rounded, the apex broadly truncate. Pronotum short and wide, narrower than the head, the anterior margin upturned, thickened, with a fine crenulate sculpture and broadly concave; the anterolateral corners upturned, thickened and projecting beyond the lateral margins; the lateral margins thickened and nearly parallel; the posterolateral corners slightly rounded; the posterior margin broadly and shallowly concave. The posterior margins of the mesonotum and metanotum as in the pronotum. Legs very short and thick, sparsely hairy; claws and spurs very short and thick; spurs serrate, 3:3:3. Measurements (mm): pronotum length 0.55, width 1.07; hind tibia length 0.66; the remaining items (body length, head length with the mandibles, head width, mandible length, width of the narrowest part of the postmentum) are incomplete in the photocopy of the original and are not transcribed.
